title: Acceptable sources for risk adjustment
question: Can this document support a diagnosis code for risk adjustment? Assign the code it supports, or 'no code' if it cannot be used.
note:
Reason for Visit
Patient presents for a nurse visit to receive education on proper inhaler technique for management of known COPD. Patient is aware of diagnosis but reports difficulty coordinating hand-breath synchronization with the device.

Vitals
BP: 132/78 mmHg
HR: 74 bpm (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 94% on RA
RR: 18
Ht/Wt: 145 lbs

Recent Labs
HbA1c: 6.2% (Date: 01/15/2026)
eGFR: 65 mL/min/1.73m2
WBC: 7.2 x 10^9/L

Review of Systems
General: Denies fever, chills, or fatigue.
Respiratory: Reports occasional shortness of breath on exertion. Denies productive cough or wheezing.
CV: Denies chest pain or palpitations.
Musculoskeletal: Denies joint pain or swelling.
Neuro: Denies dizziness or confusion.

Social History
Lives at home with spouse. Retired. Non-smoker. Independent with ADLs.

Family History
Father: Hypertension, Stroke.
Mother: Type 2 Diabetes.

Nursing Assessment
Pt is a 90-year-old male who appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. Skin is warm and dry. Lung sounds are diminished in bases but clear. Pt demonstrates poor technique with MDI, specifically failing to coordinate the puff with inhalation. Pt is able to follow multi-step instructions but requires frequent repetition due to age. No signs of acute distress noted during teaching.

Patient Education
Provided 1:1 education on MDI and spacer use. Demonstrated correct "shake, prime, and puff" technique. Instructed pt to inhale slowly and deeply while depressing canister. Pt practiced technique 5 times with successful completion each time. Educated on importance of rinsing mouth after use. Encouraged to perform deep breathing exercises twice daily.

Plan
Pt to continue current medication regimen. Pt will practice inhaler technique twice daily at home. Follow up with nursing department in 4 weeks to reassess technique and symptom management. No provider seen today.

Electronically signed, S. Patel, RN, 03/12/2026
explanations: A registered nurse is not an acceptable provider type for risk adjustment; the visit needs a physician or other acceptable clinician. No code.

distractors.why: A nurse visit alone cannot support the diagnosis.

style.document: Write a nurse visit note by a registered nurse (RN), with sections: Reason for Visit, Vitals, Nursing Assessment, Patient Education, Plan. The patient is not seen by a physician, nurse practitioner or physician assistant today.
